positions.name: AsyncJobContractAsRatifiedGoverningFact
positions.frame: What grounds the async job contract's stated behavior — a ratified decision already settled, or a case still being argued?
positions.why: All three expressions describe facets of the same ratified async job contract (receipt-in-seconds, no-blocking/no-lost-work guarantee, dispatch-then-poll-or-piggyback pattern), and each is delivered the same way: as a settled outcome of ratification rather than an argued claim — 'We ratified' performs the settling in src-1, the absolute 'no' framing in src-2 extends that settled rule rather than re-arguing it, and src-3 explicitly labels itself 'Key decision.' The register stays native pipeline vocabulary throughout (receipt, cursor, poll, piggybacked), reinforcing that these are stated as governing facts of an agreed contract, not persuasion. No tension is resolved here — the group simply reads the contract's terms as authority-by-ratification.
